title: Senior Signal Sergeant
raw_text:
10-25Z. MOS 25Z – Senior Signal Sergeant, CMF 25 (Eff 202510)
a. Major Duties. The Senior Signal Sergeant plans, coordinates, directs, and
supervises the installation, operation, and management of information technology
and telecommunication networks. Provides technical advice and assistance to
commanders, staff, and subordinate units. Coordinates Signal activities with
higher, lower, and adjacent headquarters. Performs Signal staff and senior
operations NCO functions, to include writing Signal policy, procedures,
operational plans, orders, and reports. Understands and assimilates emerging
technology to control and monitor network status within the operational
environment. Develops battlefield Signal operational plans to support
organizations at battalion and higher levels, and for Joint and Combined
Commands and activities. Operates as part of an Army modular component at
the service, joint, inter-agency, inter-governmental, and multi-national levels in
multi-domain operations.
b. MOSC 25Z5O. The Signal Master Sergeant leads, manages, and trains
company and battalion level signal activities. Provides oversight and experience
inclusive of all aspects of the Signal Warfighting Functions. Maintains Signal
readiness through organizational expertise and operational guidance in the areas
of various functions such as IT operations, signal support operations,
communication systems, strategic networks, and signal systems to the multi-
domain operations at all echelons. The Signal First Sergeant supervises the
manning, training, equipping and combat readiness of a company level of
command. Maintains unit readiness, enforces standards, and ensures the health
and welfare of Soldiers, DA Civilians, and their families across the command.
c. MOSC 25Z6O. The Signal Sergeant Major provides strategic level advice to
command and staff on all aspects of Signal operations. Supervises, plans,
coordinates, and directs Signal Multi-Domain Operations at all echelons. Mentors
command leadership and subordinate personnel on Signal functions and
capabilities. Facilitates and synchronizes joint Signal functions and capabilities
at the corps, theater, ASCC, and inter-service level and develops strategic
concepts. The Signal Command Sergeant Major coordinates and supervises
activities pertaining to organizational and strategic Signal operations. Enforces
standards of performance, training, appearance and conduct of Enlisted
personnel within the command.
d. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award of MOS. Signal
Senior Sergeant must possess the following qualifications:
       (1) Physical demands rating of Moderate.
       (2) A physical profile of 212221.
       (3) Normal color vision.
       (4) Minimum aptitude area score--N/A.
       (5) A security eligibility of SECRET is required for the initial award and to
maintain the MOS.
       (6) A U.S. citizen.
       (7) This MOS is closed for reclassification except through the normal
career progression in MOS 25B, MOS 25H, MOS 25S, or MOS 25U through
promotion.
   e. Additional skill identifiers. (Note: Refer to table 12-2 for List of universal
ASI’s associated with this MOS.)
       (1) 3C--Operational Contract Support (OCS)
       (2) 5C--Mission Command Digital Master Gunner (MCDMG)
       (3) J7--WHCA Console Control Operations.
       (4) Q6--Protection Cell Operations (skill level 4 through 6 for personnel
only) (Effective 202410).
  f. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and
SG relating to each skill level are listed in the following tables:
       (1) Table 10-25Z-1. Physical requirements.
       (2) Table 10-25Z-2 Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
       (3) Table 10-25Z-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
